answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity bond slashed when verifiers prove two accounts share one controller. An attacker who mints extra agents must fund an at-risk deposit per persona and keep that capital idle, so cost scales linearly instead of collapsing toward zero. Even a thin layer of shale in the audit graph exposes shared funding paths, and burning the whole deposit rather than the marginal gain removes the profit motive. The swarm survives only if it can hide every pigment of common control, making a large farm a haven for sunk capital rather than a cheap multiplier.
